reviews.title: High quality 1080p gaming, at an affordable price
reviews.comment: I purchased this card to replace one that was nearly 10 years old and was starting to show its age, not being able to play more modern games, such as those that require raytracing. I also didn't have a huge budget to work from so this card was right in my price range. Installation took less than 30 minutes including driver installation time. I still remember a time when Intel graphics were considered laughable in the gaming arena but it's obvious they've been working hard at catching up to AMD and NVIDIA. Despite this card's mid-range price, it performs very well. I don't have 4K monitors so 1080p gaming is all I do, so I can only speak to that performance, but games released within the last year or so run very well even with graphics quality cranked up. I don't measure frames per second, nor do I care, what matters to me is how playable a game is without stuttering, minimal lag and with quality as high as possible. Fans are quiet, even when running a graphics intensive game, my system fans drown out any noise the card tries to make. Overall, if you're in the market for an affordable yet capable graphics card, you can't go wrong with this one.
reviews.author: N. Claypool

reviews.title: Great Value
reviews.comment: This card is a great value at this price. Used it with an Intel 10700f and it plays everything at 1080p with Medium settings or better.  Even tweaked the settings to get Stalker 2 going at an acceptable rate on a widescreen monitor.  I've not had any driver problems with games, and I've tried it with a number of them.  Had a little trouble with video being scrambled after waking from sleep on the Displayports.  HDMI is fine, so there's the easy work around.  I don't know of a better deal at $170.
reviews.author: Bryan Smith

reviews.title: ASRock wins again
reviews.comment: This was used for my second build; my son's first desktop. He plays games like Minecraft, Roblox, dredge, Sandbox Universe, Minecraft Dungeons, and a few others. He consistently hits around 70fps at 1080p with no upscaling technology being used. While the card itself is a bit "large" it does work well. He seems very happy with it as it was a solid upgrade from his MSI gaming laptop that had an RTX 2050 in it. We have it connected to an ASRock MB, 32gb DDR5, and a i5-12600kf as the brain. It has exceeded his expectations and he is very happy with it. Most of all the games he plays only use around 60% of the VRam available. So hopefully it'll stand the test of time some.
reviews.author: SM
